messages:
Priya (People Ops): Heads up — need quick guidance on a contractor -> IC conversion. Manager wants an effective date that would affect proration and possibly a small retro. Questions: can we backdate pay for time they were contracting? How do equity/grant cycles handle conversions? Any payroll/benefits gotchas?
Alex W: Who's the candidate and what's the proposed band/offer?
Priya (People Ops): Contractor name is Mateo, been on contractor agreement since Nov 2025. Offer is for IC level 3 equivalent, start/offer effective 2026-04-15, base comp in offer, $6k sign-on (one-time), equity scheduled for next quarterly grant (2026-07-01). Manager asking if we can set effective 2026-04-01 to capture more pay in April and make them benefits-eligible earlier.
Maria P: Quick compops notes: conversions are generally treated like external hires for equity timing unless we approve an off-cycle grant. Retroactive salary (backpay) is not standard and requires Finance sign-off + documented justification. Sign-on timing follows the offer terms — if it says paid in first payroll after start, we follow that.
Jamal K: Can we move effective date earlier to 4/01? Manager wants PTO accrual to start sooner and to avoid waiting for next benefits window. Also worried about payroll cutoff dates.
Priya (People Ops): Payroll cutoffs: we operate on a monthly cutoff (usually the 25th). If paperwork is fully submitted and approved before the cutoff prior to the pay period, we can include the hire in that month's payroll. If not, it'll fall to the next cycle. For backpay: we need an explicit approval route (manager justification + compops + finance).
HRbot: automated: Benefits eligibility for conversions: benefits enrollment opens within 14 days of start; most plans become active 30 days after hire date. Please submit benefits enrollment within the window to avoid delay.
Maria P: Action steps I need: submit the 'Conversion Packet' via the compops form (link: https://intra.redwood/compops/conversion-form), include: - offer letter, - contractor invoices (last 3 months), - manager justification (why effective date earlier), - proposed effective date, - whether you request off-cycle equity or backpay.
Maria P: If you request retro pay, include exact dollar math and a note approving fund source. Finance reviews backpay requests and typically requires a compensation exception approval chain. Off-cycle RSUs require Exec approval for grants outside scheduled cycles.
Priya (People Ops): Also note: contractor hours billed as 1099/contractor cannot be converted to salary retroactively without a taxable correction — compops will coordinate with Payroll/Finance on how any approved backpay is processed.
Alex W: Got it. I'll collect invoices + manager note. If we want expedite, what's the fastest turnaround we can expect? :pray:
Priya (People Ops): If you mark the form subject with [EXPEDITE] and attach complete docs we triage within 48 business hours. Finance approvals still vary but we'll flag it. Also cc compops@redwood.com on the submission.
Jamal K: Thanks — will submit tonight. One last Q: any difference if contractor was on our SOW vs through agency?
Maria P: Yes — agency contractors have additional vendor/agency terms; conversion paperwork needs vendor offboarding notes. Include the agency contract release if applicable.
Priya (People Ops): Thanks everyone. I'll follow up once compops confirms receipt. :+1:
